q: Oligomycin blocks the proton channel of ATP synthase. What happens to electron transport and O2 consumption in treated mitochondria?
options: Both increase, because protons can no longer leak back into the matrix through ATP synthase
Both fall: the gradient grows until pumps can't push H+ against it, so electron flow slows
Electron transport carries on as normal, but oxygen consumption by complex IV stops completely
Neither changes at all; only the output of ATP from ATP synthase falls
explanation: Electron transport and ATP synthesis are coupled through the gradient. With H+ unable to return through ATP synthase, the gradient becomes so steep that pumping needs more energy than electron transfer releases; electron flow slows, NADH accumulates and O2 use falls (respiratory control). Adding an uncoupler such as DNP restarts O2 use – but without ATP synthesis.
